Worth internalising as a shape: when you're building something up across iterations, the loop body's job is to mutate the accumulator and the function's job is to hand it back once the loop has finished, so the return belongs at the function's indentation level, not the body's. The three keywords are easy to blur when you're moving fast — continue abandons this iteration, break abandons the loop, return abandons the function — and only the third one is what you want after the work is done.
